strategy.summary: Reproduce GH#68573: SparseArray.astype to a dense target densifies via np.asarray(self), which picks the output dtype from type(fill_value) rather than its value. For uint64 values with an int fill_value, np.result_type(uint64, int) = float64, silently rounding values above 2**53 (2**63+12345 becomes 9223372036854788096, off by 57). Boxed pd.Timestamp/pd.Timedelta fill values make the densified array object dtype (raw int64), causing garbage dates, TypeError for int64 targets, or mixed boxed/raw object values. Fix routes densification through _densify().

input_output_examples.input: ser.astype("uint64").to_numpy() where ser = pd.Series(np.array([1, 0, big], dtype="uint64")).astype(pd.SparseDtype("uint64", 0)) and big = 2**63 + 12345

input_output_examples.buggy_output: TypeError for the int64 target; object dtype held raw int64, giving a garbage date after a unit change and mixed boxed/raw values for object
input_output_examples.expected_output: pd.array(values).astype(dtype) (exact stored values; equals expected via tm.assert_equal)

input_output_examples.buggy_output: TypeError for the int64 target; object dtype held raw int64 (garbage timedelta / mixed boxed and raw values)

strategy.summary: Reproduce PR#68464's numerical bug in pandas.core.nanops: nanvar/nanstd/nansem apply an explicit boolean mask only in the denominator (count/d), while the masked entry's non-NaN value still enters the mean, so masked positions do not propagate NaN under skipna=False. Also bool input is not cast to f8, so np.nan putmask can be truthy. Reproduction = check out buggy commit 1f32fb44c03b9a5badc441898d0ac76a8c4db08a, build pandas (Meson/meson-python, Cython>=3.1.0,<4, Python 3.11), add the PR's tests to pandas/tests/test_nanops.py, and observe the mask/NaN assertions fail; they pass at fixed commit 60f04b68f0f6756106e3e8728537b0412acb4de9.

input_output_examples.input: values = np.array([[1.0, 1.0], [np.nan, 2.0], [3.0, 3.0]]); mask = np.array([[False, False], [True, True], [False, False]]); nanops.nanvar(values, axis=0, skipna=False, mask=mask)
nanops.nanvar(np.array([[1, 1], [5, 2], [3, 0]], dtype='f8'), mask=np.array([[False, False], [True, False], [False, False]]), skipna=False, axis=0)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: result[0] is NOT NaN; the masked value 5 still enters the column-0 mean (assert np.isnan(result[0]) fails)
input_output_examples.expected_output: np.isnan(result[0]) is True and not np.isnan(result[1]) (NaN only in the slice holding the mask)

input_output_examples.input: nanops.nanvar(np.array([[1, 1], [5, 2], [3, 0]], dtype='f8'), mask=np.array([[False, False], [True, False], [False, False]]), skipna=False, axis=None)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: np.isnan(result) is False (masked 5 still in the mean, no NaN propagated)
input_output_examples.expected_output: np.isnan(result) is True (whole reduction covers the masked entry)

input_output_examples.input: nanops.nanstd / nanops.nansem(np.array([[1, 1], [5, 2], [3, 0]], dtype=dtype), mask=np.array([[False, False], [True, False], [False, False]]), skipna=False, axis in {None, 0}) for dtype in f8,f4,i8,u8,bool,c16,O
input_output_examples.buggy_output: axis=None: not NaN; axis=0: result[0] not NaN (mask only in denominator; bool input also not cast to f8, so np.nan putmask is truthy)
input_output_examples.expected_output: axis=None: np.isnan(result); axis=0: np.isnan(result[0]) and not np.isnan(result[1])

input_output_examples.input: nanops.nanvar|nanstd|nansem(np.arange(25, dtype=np.float64).reshape(5, 5), mask=mask, skipna=False, axis=axis) with mask=np.zeros((5,5),bool); mask[0,0]=True; axis in {0,1}
input_output_examples.buggy_output: result[0] is not NaN for nanvar/nanstd (mask applied only in denominator, masked grid value still enters the mean)
input_output_examples.expected_output: np.isnan(result[0]) True, not np.isnan(result[1:]).any(), and np.isnan(result) matches nanops.nanskew(values, mask=mask, skipna=False, axis=axis)

input_output_examples.input: nanops.nanvar|nanstd|nansem(np.array([[1, 1], [5, 2], [3, 0]], dtype=dtype), mask=np.array([[False, False], [True, True], [False, False]]), skipna=True, axis in {None, 0})
input_output_examples.buggy_output: n/a - the skipna=True path already drops the masked entry from both numerator and denominator, so this test is expected to pass on the buggy commit

strategy.expected_buggy_behavior: With an explicit mask and skipna=False, nanvar/nanstd/nansem return non-NaN values at slices containing a masked (non-NaN) entry: the masked position is dropped from count/d and zeroed in the squared-deviation sum, but its value still enters the mean. So np.isnan(result[0]) (axis=0/1) and np.isnan(result) (axis=None) are False where NaN is expected; bool input is also not cast to f8, so np.nan putmask can be truthy.
strategy.expected_fixed_behavior: Masked entries propagate NaN under skipna=False into every result covering them and only into those slices (matching nanskew): axis=None -> np.isnan(result); axis=0/1 -> np.isnan(result[0]) and not np.isnan(result[1]). Under skipna=True the masked entry drops out of both numerator and denominator, so the result equals the operation on values with masked rows removed. Fixed nanops fills masked positions with NaN under skipna=False (0 under skipna=True) and casts bool into the i/u->f8 path.
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy commit, the reproduction tests fail (assert np.isnan(result[0]) / assert np.isnan(result) raise for nanvar/nanstd/nansem with a mask and skipna=False), and the same selector passes once the nanops.py fix is applied.
risks_or_ambiguities: The three tests are new/modified in the PR; at the buggy commit they must be injected from the PR test diff, otherwise pytest reports 'no tests ran'/collection errors instead of a failing assertion.

strategy.summary: Reproduce GH#49631: casting a datetime64/timedelta64 SparseArray to an integer or boolean Sparse dtype (e.g. arr.astype("Sparse[int64]")) at buggy commit 6ce79779 silently replaces the dtype's fill_value with the target default (0/False) instead of converting the source fill value. The PR adds new tests in pandas/tests/arrays/sparse/test_astype.py that assert the converted fill value; at this revision those tests must FAIL.

input_output_examples.input: values = np.array([1, 1, 2], dtype="M8[ns]"); arr = SparseArray(values, fill_value=np.datetime64(values[0])); arr.astype("Sparse[int64]")
input_output_examples.buggy_output: fill_value silently replaced with the target default 0, i.e. dtype resolves to pd.SparseDtype("int64", fill_value=0)
input_output_examples.expected_output: pd.SparseDtype("int64", fill_value=values[0].astype("int64")) and data values.astype("int64"); same for the pandas-boxed fill spellings (pd.Timestamp / pd.Timedelta)

input_output_examples.input: values = np.array(["NaT", 1, 2], dtype="M8[ns]"); arr = SparseArray(values, dtype=pd.SparseDtype("M8[ns]", pd.NaT)); arr.astype("Sparse[int64]")
input_output_examples.buggy_output: raises (pd.NaT spelling does not convert the way the numpy NaT spelling does)

input_output_examples.input: values = np.array([1, 2, 3], dtype="M8[ns]"); arr = SparseArray(values, fill_value=np.datetime64(5, "ns")); arr.sp_index.npoints == len(arr); arr.astype("Sparse[int64]")
input_output_examples.buggy_output: on a fully dense array the fill_value is not converted (silently 0) rather than 5
input_output_examples.expected_output: result.dtype == pd.SparseDtype("int64", fill_value=5) and result.to_dense() equals values.astype("int64")

input_output_examples.input: values = np.array([1, 1, 2], dtype="M8[ns]"); arr = SparseArray(values, fill_value=values[0]); arr.astype("Sparse[bool]")
input_output_examples.buggy_output: result.dtype == pd.SparseDtype(bool, fill_value=False)
input_output_examples.expected_output: result.dtype == pd.SparseDtype(bool, fill_value=True) (the fill value's truthiness)

input_output_examples.input: dti = pd.date_range("2016-01-01", periods=3); ser[0] = pd.NaT; sparse = pd.core.arrays.SparseArray(ser.values); sparse.astype("Sparse[int64]")
input_output_examples.expected_output: the fill_value must not silently become 0; it should be converted from NaT (or raise as the reporter expected)

strategy.summary: At buggy commit bd801af80f5a2f873cc7bd93d04ebc638698de9c, HDFStore.select(where=...) applies ordering comparisons ('<','<=','>','>=') directly to the int64 representation of datetime64/timedelta64 columns and the index. Since NaT is stored as iNaT (int64 min), it sorts below every real timestamp, so '<'/'<=' predicates wrongly match NaT rows. Pandas' pytables.BinOp.generate lacks the ((col != iNaT) & (col <op> val)) guard. Reproduce by installing pandas editable with PyTables+numexpr, adding the PR's test hunks to the buggy checkout, and running the two new select tests plus the modified test_append_with_timedelta, which fail with tm.assert_frame_equal shape/value mismatches because NaT rows are returned.

strategy.summary: At buggy commit b750c9ba, get_unit_for_round in pandas/_libs/tslibs/timedeltas.pyx converts a requested freq into the object's resolution with round_ok=True, silently truncating freqs not exactly representable at that resolution. round/floor/ceil on Timestamp/DatetimeIndex/Timedelta with such a freq (e.g. '2500ms' or '700ms' on second-resolution data) do NOT raise the documented ValueError and instead round at the wrong granularity. Repro is via the PR-added test pandas/tests/reshape/test_qcut.py::test_qcut_contains plus the issue example pd.qcut([0,1,2,3], 3, precision=0). Success = the assertion `value in bucket` fails on the buggy commit.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: assert value in bucket fails for the value(s) landing exactly on a miscomputed quantile boundary
input_output_examples.expected_output: assert value in bucket passes for all parametrizations (scale in [1.0, 1/3, 17.0], q in [3, 7, 9], precision in [1, 3, 16])
